text:
incident-bot: PAGE: 2141594321 - cluster infer-prod-usw2 reporting node heartbeat instability (multiple NotReady). Severity: P1
sara: picked up. oncall lead here. creating PD ticket PD-9001 and paging infra/runtime.
sara: running quick node check - `kubectl get nodes -l role=inference -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.conditions[-1].type,AGE:.metadata.age`
sara: results: 32 total nodes, 7 reporting NotReady, 3 in Unknown state.
omar: grabbing journal logs from affected host infer-node-09 — seeing kubelet restart loops and kernel OOMs. snippet:
omar: ```
Mar 20 03:12:44 infer-node-09 kubelet[2123]: E0320 03:12:44.987654 kubelet_kuberuntime_manager.go:xxx] "container start failed" err="rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start container: exit status 137"
Mar 20 03:12:45 infer-node-09 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 18237 (inference-server) total-vm:...kB
```
mike: sounds like memory pressure + kubelet churn. priority actions: cordon affected nodes, drain gracefully, bump nodepool, collect OOM and GPU logs.
sara: cordoning now: `kubectl cordon infer-node-09` 
sara: draining with `kubectl drain infer-node-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`
deploy-bot: autoscaler: detected pending inference pods -> provisioning 8 additional nodes (current target 40 -> 48).
julia: routing: temporarily shifting 25% traffic from infer-prod-usw2 to eu-west-1 pool. will monitor error rates.
omar: on some pods I see `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` right before they OOM. attaching stack traces and container logs to PD-9001.
mike: infra, can you confirm if the recent nvidia-driver push went to these nodes? @infra-team
infra-team: confirmed. drivers were updated last weekend to 530.41. We have a small set of nodes on the older 525 in other pools.
mike: ok, plan: 1) cordon/drain the 7 NotReady nodes (sara/mike) 2) hold new driver rollout to remaining nodes 3) scale nodepool up to absorb traffic 4) route critical customers to eu-west fallback 5) capture GPU logs and potential coredumps 6) create INF-7204 for infra deep-dive.
sara: I'll hand off incident owner to mike at 03:30 for extended infra work. staying until drains complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
mike: taking over. I'm going to toggle `vm.overcommit_memory=1` on the affected hosts and raise kubelet eviction thresholds temporarily to avoid cascading evictions. Will also disable automatic rolling upgrades for inference node pools.
omar: enabling additional prefix and KV cache on healthy nodes to reduce per-request token generation while we recover. low-risk and reversible.
sara: customer-impact quick check: p50 latency up ~80ms, 5xx rate peaked at 3.1% for us-west endpoints; premium customers saw some retries but no SLO breaches yet. tagging PD accordingly.
julia: telemetry shows the error spike dropping after drains and routing changes to ~0.6%. keeping canary at 25%.
mike: two of the NotReady nodes are not reachable via SSH - likely kernel panic or network meltdown. infra is powering them off and reprovisioning.
infractrl-bot: note: reprovision jobs queued for infer-node-11 and infer-node-14. ETA ~4m.
omar: collecting `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, and kubelet logs. also requesting `crash` analyzer on any cores in /var/crash.
sara: PD-9001 update: severity remains high; acknowledged by sara at 03:14; ownership moving to mike at 03:30.
mike: infra reports the driver package has a memory leak in 530.41 under certain CUDA workloads. rolling back drivers on reprovisioned nodes to 525.85 as temporary mitigation.
julia: after driver rollback and routing changes, error rate stabilized around baseline. continuing to watch.
deploy-bot: automatic service fallback to compatible lower-memory model variants enabled for affected routing rules.
mike: follow-ups: 1) driver rollback for pool, 2) add preflight tests for driver+runtime under high-concurrency, 3) add kubelet OOM early-detection alert, 4) tune eviction thresholds and document temporary knobs. opening INF-7204 and assigning to infra/runtime teams.
omar: runtime item: add detection for `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` and trigger faster failover to warm replicas to reduce customer impact.
sara: handoff complete. closing immediate page at 03:46 as error rates normalized. leaving INF-7204 / PD-9001 open for RCA and action items. filing postmortem draft and assigning owners. :white_check_mark: 
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: PD-9001 marked as resolved (page closed) at 03:46, follow-up tasks in INF-7204 and PD-9001.
